title: AI Bubble Risks Worst S&P 500 Crash Since 2008, Strategist Says
source_used: Bloomberg text read on Yahoo Finance UK copy (bloomberg.com returned 403)
key_facts: Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at Panmure Liberum, a London investment bank, says the AI bubble will burst in 2027 or 2028.
His 2027 year-end target of 5,000 points for the S&P 500 implies 36% downside from current levels.
He is the most bearish of seven other strategists tracked by Bloomberg, who on average look for 14% upside.
He says hyperscalers' free cash flows are largely depleted and the cost of debt is rising quickly.
He acknowledges his bearish call may be premature and advises clients to prepare contingency plans rather than sell now.
Bloomberg Intelligence estimates hyperscaler data-centre spending in 2026 could more than double from last year to $713 billion.
quote_evidence: "My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years," Klement said in an interview.

Klement acknowledges that his bearish call may be premature and he remains the most bullish among Bloomberg-tracked strategists for the Stoxx 600 until the end of 2026, predicting gains of about 10% in the regional benchmark.
why_it_matters_hint: One strategist's bear case warns that AI spending and debt could end an equity rally, a risk to investors and savers.
event_date: Not stated (Bloomberg dated 8 Oct 2026; 'this week' in the article)
notes: Read on the Yahoo Finance UK copy of the Bloomberg text. The headline is close to the article's 'could trigger the most severe market crash since the global financial crisis' and is kept. He is one of eight strategists tracked, and he says his call may be premature.
